### Chatham County

- **Type:** County
- **Status:** 🟢 Active
- **Date enacted:** 2026-02-11
- **Normalized date:** `2026-02-11` (exact)
- **Duration:** 12 months, to 2027-02-11, or earlier if new zoning regulations are adopted
- **Current end date:** `2027-02-11`
- **Sectors:** data center, cryptocurrency mining
- **Moratorium ID:** `nc-chatham-county-2026`
- **Legal basis:** Ordinance 26-0061; N.C.G.S. 160D-107; hearing under N.C.G.S. 160D-601
- **What prompted it:** Potential large-scale data center interest at Triangle Innovation Point West in Moncure; county findings cite water and electricity use, greenhouse gas emissions, pollution, e-waste, noise, and unaddressed zoning categories.
- **Affected projects:** Triangle Innovation Point West; ordinance covers data centers, data processing facilities, cryptocurrency mining operations, and related uses in unincorporated Chatham County outside municipal ETJs.
- **Detailed status:** Active as of 2026-09-23 until 2027-02-11 (or earlier adoption of zoning rules). On 2026-09-17 Superior Court Judge John Morris granted summary judgment to Eco TIP West, LLC in its suit against Chatham County, holding its 750 MW Triangle Innovation Point West data center project may proceed notwithstanding the moratorium (exemption under N.C.G.S. 160D-107(c) / vested rights) and ordering a damages determination; the moratorium itself remains in force for other projects.
- **Outcome:** Pending. Staff studying impacts and preparing zoning text amendments; the Eco TIP West project was held exempt by court order on 2026-09-17, with damages to be determined.

### Cherokee County (high-impact facilities; cryptocurrency mining; data-center-adjacent)

- **Type:** County
- **Status:** ⚪ Expired
- **Date enacted:** 2023-10-02 (signed by Chairman Cal Stiles, Cherokee County Board of Commissioners; "On this the 2nd day of October, 2023" per OCR of the High Impact Facility Moratorium PDF).
- **Normalized date:** `2023-10-02` (exact)
- **Duration:** 1 year from date of adoption, "or until such time as the Cherokee County Board of Commissioners enacts a high-impact land use ordinance," per Section 3 of the ordinance (OCR-confirmed).
- **Current end date:** `—`
- **Sectors:** cryptocurrency mining, data center
- **Moratorium ID:** `nc-cherokee-county-2023`
- **Legal basis:** High-Impact Facility Moratorium adopted under N.C.G.S. 160D-107(a) and 160D-107(d); ordinance text recites Cherokee County Comprehensive Plan adoption September 18, 2023 and finds at least 3 crypto mining sites in the county; covered uses include asphalt facilities; bulk inflammable, chemical, biological-waste or explosive storage; cryptocurrency mining server farms; unenclosed data storage facilities with powered cooling; facilities with generators ≥600 kW fossil-fuel power; solid-waste management/disposal facilities; commercial incinerators; bulk concrete production; nuclear/toxic-material storage or disposal; and privately operated prisons. Scope: unincorporated Cherokee County, excluding lands within the Qualla Boundary of the Eastern Band of Cherokee Indians. The county does not have land-use zoning, so the moratorium operated through permit gating only. PDF stored at `research/_originals/cherokee-county-high-impact-facility-moratorium-2023.pdf`; OCR text in `research/_web/cherokee-county-high-impact-facility-moratorium-2023-ocr.md`.
- **What prompted it:** Existing cryptocurrency mining noise and electricity concerns in the Murphy/Marble area.
- **Affected projects:** Cryptocurrency mining/high-impact facilities; the Marble facility has converted from crypto to AI workloads.
- **Detailed status:** Expired — per BPR (2026-04-10), the Cherokee County moratorium "had been expired for a year" by January 2026; Commissioner Ben Adams asked the board to renew the moratorium and add AI data centers, but the board did not act, and Adams is now pursuing planning-board-led ordinance work (per Cherokee Scout). One former crypto mine in Marble (Core Scientific) is converting to a hyperscaler-class AI data center.
- **Outcome:** No moratorium currently in force; planning board reconvened to develop possible ordinance without zoning.

### City of Brevard

- **Type:** City

### City of Kings Mountain

- **Type:** City
- **Status:** 🟢 Extended
- **Date enacted:** 2026-02-24
- **Normalized date:** `2026-02-24` (exact)
- **Duration:** Originally 182 days (2026-02-24 to 2026-08-25); extended on 2026-08-25 for an additional twelve months, to about 2027-08-25, unless ended earlier by council
- **Current end date:** `2027-08-25`
- **Sectors:** data center

Dissenting: Neisler, Fletcher. Extended 2026-08-25 by a further ordinance 'to extend the existing moratorium on permitting new data centers for an additional twelve months' (agenda item 10D), adopted 6-1 (Neisler dissenting); extension ordinance number not published in materials located.

- **Affected projects:** No named project in captured agenda packet.
- **Detailed status:** Extended; active as of 2026-09-23. On 2026-08-25, the day the original 182-day moratorium expired, City Council voted 6-1 (Councilmember Scott Neisler dissenting) to extend the moratorium on permitting new data centers for twelve more months, to about 2027-08-25, while staff finish UDO data center standards. An 80-acre AI data center proposal off I-85 remains on hold; the existing T5 campus is unaffected.
- **Outcome:** Extended 12 months on 2026-08-25; UDO text amendments for data centers still in preparation with the Planning and Zoning Board.

- **Legal basis:** Vance County 60-day data center moratorium (number not located), N.C.G.S. 160D-107; the legal notice advertised 60 days, so a 6-month motion was ruled out of order
- **What prompted it:** Natelli Holdings filed a preliminary plan for a 900 MW, 12-building data center campus on ~530 acres along U.S. 158 while the county revises its UDO data center rules
- **Affected projects:** Natelli Holdings 900 MW data center campus (Technology Lane / U.S. 158).
- **Detailed status:** Active as of 2026-09-23; 60-day moratorium adopted 2026-09-14, ending 2026-11-13 or on adoption of the pending zoning text amendment.
- **Outcome:** 60-day moratorium pending UDO text amendment.

### Watauga County

- **Type:** County
- **Status:** 🟢 Active
- **Date enacted:** 2026-04-21, Board of Commissioners meeting; Board voted unanimously to adopt a one-year countywide data center moratorium at this meeting (Watauga Democrat).
- **Normalized date:** `2026-04-21` (unverified)
- **Duration:** One year (adopted 2026-04-21; to about 2027-04-21)
- **Current end date:** `2027-04-21`
- **Sectors:** data center
- **Moratorium ID:** `nc-watauga-county-2026`
- **Legal basis:** County data center moratorium proposed under N.C.G.S. 160D-107. [Evidence ceiling: Watauga County's BOC agendas/minutes archives at wataugacounty.org/App_Pages/Dept/BOC/{agendas,minutes}.aspx confirmed via real-Chrome fetch on 2026-04-30 to contain zero 2026 records.]
- **What prompted it:** Regional data center concern after March 23 Boone action; Director Walker testified small data centers can consume 1–10 MW (700–7,000 homes) and large facilities use 1.5 million gallons of water per day, with Watauga lacking the power capacity to absorb such load.
- **Affected projects:** None named in Watauga Democrat reporting.
- **Detailed status:** Active as of 2026-09-23; the Board of Commissioners unanimously adopted a one-year countywide data center moratorium on 2026-04-21 (to about 2027-04-21). No rescission or replacement found; the county still has not posted 2026 Board minutes online (latest posted minutes are from July 2025).
- **Outcome:** Pending UDO process; commissioners directed staff to develop comprehensive regulations within the moratorium year.
